raw_segments.text: Grandpré, Why do you stay so long, my lords of France? Yond Island carrions, desperate
of their bones, ill-favourately become the morning field. Their ragged curtains poorly
are let loose, and our air shakes them passing scornfully.
Big Mars seems bankrupt in their beggared host, and faintly through a rusty beaver peeps.
The horsemen sit like fixed candlesticks with torch staves in their hand, and their poor
jades lob down their heads, drooping the hides and hips, the gum downroping from their pale
dead eyes, and in their pale dull mouths the gimel bit lies foul with chewed grass, still
and motionless, and their executors, the navish crows, fly over them, all impatient for their
hour. Description cannot suit itself in words to demonstrate the life of such a battle,
in life so lifeless as it shows itself.
